title: Netflix Buys a ‘Hot Ones’ Spinoff
partialText: The streaming giant bought a spinoff of a popular online interview series that features celebrities eating fiery chicken wings, the latest salvo in its rivalry with YouTube.

title: In Alan Greenspan, Kevin Warsh Saw a Fed Chairman Role Model
partialText: Kevin M. Warsh has long singled out Alan Greenspan, who died on Monday, as the central banker he wants to exemplify.

title: YouTube Stars Take Center Stage at Creative Artists Agency
partialText: For years, creators were on the fringes at Creative Artists Agency, a Hollywood talent behemoth. Now the agency is putting them center stage.

title: Clive Davis, Music Industry Titan Who Signed Whitney Houston, Dies at 94
partialText: He rose from a midlevel position at Columbia Records to become one of music’s most powerful executives, shepherding stars like Barry Manilow and Whitney Houston.

title: ‘The View’ Asks Its Audience for Help in Battle With F.C.C.
partialText: The daytime TV talk show is at the center of a dispute with the Federal Communications Commission over political speech.

title: U.K. Markets React Calmly to Starmer Resignation, but Economic Uncertainties Linger
partialText: Markets reacted calmly to the prime minister’s announcement, which laid out a timeline for succession. Still, there’s not much clarity about the next government.

title: U.S. Oil Is Skipping the Chance to Grab Market Share From the Gulf
partialText: U.S. oil production is expected to grow only modestly next year as companies hesitate to spend more in an uncertain market.

title: Is China Closing the A.I. Gap Faster Than Expected?
partialText: Silicon Valley and corporate America are increasingly turning to cheaper, open-source artificial intelligence models built in China.

title: China Tightens Rare-Earth Grip on U.S. Firms, Threatening Trade Clash
partialText: The move targets two U.S. manufacturers at the center of the Trump administration’s effort to rebuild the domestic supply chain for critical magnets.

title: Oil Prices Fall as U.S.-Iran Talks Show Signs of Progress
partialText: Oil prices retreated after Iran’s foreign minister said there had been “major progress” toward ending the fighting in Lebanon during the first session of high-level talks.

title: Oil Rises Amid Uncertainty Over Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Modest reactions in the oil and financial markets as Iran and the U.S. met in Switzerland for a first round of talks aimed at making a temporary cease-fire permanent.

title: Tesla Driver Using Autopilot Crashes Into Home in Texas and Kills a Woman, Officials Say
partialText: The driver told investigators he was using the vehicle’s automated-driver system when the vehicle left the roadway and crashed into a house in Harris County, Texas.

title: ‘Toy Story 5’ Fuels Hollywood’s Hottest Summer Since 2019
partialText: The Disney-Pixar sequel was expected to make $160 million in North America over the weekend, lifting the summer box office to $1.85 billion to date.

title: While the World Scrambles for Oil, China Sits on Full Tanks
partialText: The possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz may not prompt China to return quickly to prewar levels of oil purchases from the Persian Gulf.

title: When a Job Goes From Dreamy to Dreary
partialText: Plus, should I follow through on complaints about one workplace after I’ve moved on to another?

title: Is Your Vibe ‘High-Signal’ or ‘Anti-Signal’?
partialText: Subtle cues are shaping notions of what’s hot and what’s not in the tech world.

title: Ina Garten to Start a Podcast With Vox Media
partialText: A new show from Ina Garten, a longtime Food Network star, spurred a bidding war, as the lines between video podcasts and talk shows blur.

title: The Latest in College Pricing: Tuition at 10 Percent of Your Income
partialText: Whitman College is trying to keep it simple: Tell us your adjusted gross income, and we won’t make you apply and get in just to receive a price quote.

title: How Remote Work Has Helped a Generation of Working Parents
partialText: Post-pandemic, a new openness to accommodating family needs has made it possible for more mothers and fathers to balance work and parenting — particularly mothers of young children.

title: Mines, Logistics and Deep Uncertainty Threaten a Middle East Oil Rebound
partialText: More oil is getting out of the Persian Gulf, but the region’s producers are looking for signs that it is safe as they ramp up plans for alternative routes.

title: Egg Prices Are Way Down, but That’s Hurting Farmers
partialText: An oversupply of hens has lowered wholesale egg prices. But consumers may not reap the full benefits because of producer contracts and higher costs.

title: The Giant Test Kitchen Where Cooks Battle A.I. Slop
partialText: People Inc., the home of Food & Wine and Southern Living, publishes more food content than anyone else. It’s pushing back against the bots with recipes from its culinary hub.

title: Cottage Cheese Shortages Are Driven by TikTok and ‘Protein-Maxxing’
partialText: TikTok and “protein-maxxing” are driving a cottage cheese squeeze that’s left some consumers desperate.

title: A Humble 3-Wheel Electric Vehicle Lands Toyota in Federal Court
partialText: A lawsuit filed in California claims the automaker’s philanthropic arm stole technology intended to help poor farmers, but it is not clear to what end.

title: For New Car Brands, the Path to Success Is Littered With Flops
partialText: Honda and Sony have bailed on Afeela, their joint E.V. project, without selling a single car. Subbrands from big automakers have a shaky track record, but leaning into luxury can help.

title: Amazon’s Movie Arm Abandons Film About OpenAI
partialText: The company, which invested $50 billion in the artificial intelligence start-up this year, will let the team behind the film, “Artificial,” try to sell the project to another studio.

title: For India, the Return of Iranian Oil Cannot Come Soon Enough
partialText: After months of shortages and uncertainty, India sees an opportunity to restore a once-crucial energy relationship.

title: Rates on New Student Loans Will Rise on July 1
partialText: Higher interest rates take effect on July 1 for the next school year. Borrowers are already dealing with rising college costs and inflation elsewhere.

title: Oil Prices Rise as U.S.-Iran Deal Faces Tests
partialText: Oil remains on track for a second straight weekly decline, but signs of cracks in the agreement to end the war have given traders pause.

title: Stranded Ships Hoping for Escape Find a Turbulent Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Shipping companies had hoped to get their vessels out after this week’s U.S.-Iran deal but faced uncertainty on Friday as violence flared again in the region.

title: How Deal With U.S. Could Reconnect Iran to the Global Economy
partialText: The country has long faced some of the world’s heaviest sanctions. The lifting of restrictions could open new vistas on trade and financial access.

title: Congress Is Anxious as U.S.-Canada-Mexico Trade Talks Intensify
partialText: With midterms approaching and negotiations heating up, some lawmakers are apprehensive over where the discussions are headed.

title: How Much Is SpaceX Really Worth?
partialText: The company’s deep commitment to Mars colonization and Elon Musk’s nearly total control make SpaceX stock an astonishingly speculative bet, our columnist says.

title: Colby College Is Stepping In to Save a Maine Town After Disaster
partialText: A new rescuer — Colby College, bankrolled by a construction magnate — will vastly change not just the economics of Port Clyde, Maine, but also its cultural and physical fabric.

title: A Viral Knicks Moment, Brought to You by a Prediction Market
partialText: What do a Jalen Brunson look-alike contest, a buzzy catchphrase and a dancing robot outside Madison Square Garden have in common?

title: Have You Bought a Tesla Recently? We Want to Hear From You.
partialText: Tesla sales are rebounding in Europe even though many people have negative feelings about Elon Musk, the company’s chief executive. We want to know why.

title: The Washington Outlet NOTUS Won’t Be ‘The Star’ After All
partialText: The publication is abandoning a planned rebranding after resolving a trademark dispute with the new publisher of The Washington Star.

title: Are You a Recent College Graduate Who Moved Back Home? We Want to Hear From You.
partialText: If you lived with your parents for nine months or more after graduation, please tell us how you came to the decision and whether the job market influenced your thinking.

title: Federal Energy Regulator Seeks to Limit Conflicts Over Data Centers
partialText: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission directed grid managers to make changes that protect individuals from higher electricity bills while giving data centers access to power faster.

title: Penske Media Is Buying What’s Left of Vox Media
partialText: The deal will put online publications like Popsugar and Eater under the same roof as Rolling Stone and Variety.

title: Education Department Lowers Student Loan Interest Rates for Two Years
partialText: The department, citing high defaults, is reducing interest rates by up to one percentage point for two years if borrowers pay automatically.

title: Warsh Wants the Fed to Send Fewer Signals. That Comes With Risks.
partialText: Investors piled on bets for higher borrowing costs after Kevin Warsh opted against providing policy guidance at his first meeting as Federal Reserve chairman.

title: Warsh’s Hawkish Turn Has Scrambled the Math on Rates
partialText: The futures market now sees at least one interest rate increase this year, as the Federal Reserve’s new leader, Kevin Warsh, vows to fight inflation.

title: Inflation Will Linger Despite U.S.-Iran Deal, British Officials Warn
partialText: Bank of England policymakers kept interest rates on hold, saying the impact of the war in Iran was still a major source of uncertainty for the economy.

title: As India Temporarily Bans Telegram, Which Other Countries Have Restricted the Messaging App?
partialText: Several countries have restricted the messaging app, a valuable platform for dissidents, criminals and extremists. Here’s an overview.

title: The Small Investors Behind SpaceX’s Stock Rally
partialText: The company’s blockbuster trading debut is the latest example of how individual investors have become a force in financial markets.

title: All Aboard! Brands Jump on the Knicks Bandwagon.
partialText: Companies — including some with no ties to New York or basketball — have posted memes, changed their avatars to Knicks blue and orange, and cheered the team in their captions.

title: Why Flight Prices Might Not Fall After the U.S.-Iran Deal
partialText: Jet fuel may stay expensive for months, and airlines know travelers are willing to pay more for tickets.

title: What to Know Before Buying SpaceX Stock, According to Financial Advisers
partialText: SpaceX has rapidly become one of the world’s most valuable companies. Even so, experts say investing in single stocks can be risky.

title: They Booked an Airbnb Ahead of the World Cup. Can a Host Demand They Pay More?
partialText: A family booked early for a big soccer trip to Southern California, then a new host suddenly raised the price. Why did Airbnb leave them in the lurch?
